races.title: State Assembly, District 74
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Sergio Farias
cands.bio: Three-term San Juan Capistrano city councilmember and twice mayor, chosen by his council colleagues. Chief operating officer of a commercial landscaping business. He previously owned and ran his late father's landscaping business for 18 years, starting at age 16. Democratic candidate for Assembly District 74.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, California Young Democrats, Equality California, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund.
In his Ballotpedia survey he also lists the California Latino Legislative Caucus, SEIU California, the California Federation of Teachers, Rep. Mike Levin, and state Sen. Tom Umberg, among others.

cands.gaps: We found no news coverage or official records of how Farias voted on the San Juan Capistrano City Council, so we can't show his record on data centers, property taxes, growth and land use, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. We found no documented statements from him on data centers or development. His claim of an 85% drop in homelessness comes only from his campaign site and is unverified. We found no reporting on controversies. His move-in date and the details of his upbringing are not documented beyond his campaign site.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site describes him as a homegrown leader who was born and raised in the San Juan Capistrano neighborhoods he serves, the son of immigrants who settled there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Three-term San Juan Capistrano city councilmember since 2016 and twice mayor. He owned and operated a landscaping business for 18 years and is now COO of a commercial landscaping company.
qual.why: Local elected office plus business ownership and management fits the middle band. He has no state legislative service and no documented policy or budget career.

cands.name: Laurie Davies
cands.bio: Republican Assemblymember for District 74 in southern Orange County, first elected in 2020. Owns Five Star Wedding & Events, founded in 2000. Earlier worked as a restaurant general manager. Served on the Laguna Niguel City Council from 2012 and was mayor. Sat on the Orange County Fire Authority board.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Republican Party of California (listed for 2024 and 2026).

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Davies on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, donor money, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no documented public stances on data centers or development. The only policy item found is that she organized a letter-writing coalition urging regional air regulators to reject rules phasing out natural-gas space and water heaters, which does not map to any of those topics. Her birth city in Wisconsin and her exact date of arrival in Orange County after college were not found. Her Ballotpedia endorsements list was unclear on which endorsements are formal, so we left out those we could not confirm as official.

local.label: Roots 55: She was born and raised in Wisconsin and moved to California in 1981 to attend Cal State Long Beach, and has lived in Orange County since, which is more than 25 years as an adult resident.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State Assemblymember since 2020; Laguna Niguel city councilmember from 2012 and mayor; Orange County Fire Authority board member from 2017; owner of an events business since 2000; former restaurant general manager.
qual.why: She has about six years of prior legislative service in the Assembly, plus local elected office and business ownership. No law, policy or budget career was found, so the score sits at the low end of the high range.
